problem: Providers exiting before initialization could be silently retained as closed and repeatedly respawned for pending work, leaving accepted tasks without a terminal result. Seen during real Codex argument-error acceptance.
implementation: Track successful initialization and first task admission independently for each owned Pi/Codex/Claude lifetime.
After confirmed process-tree exit and drained stdout, classify an uninitialized unused lifetime as a typed startup failure, including exit code 0.
Persist startup fault with existing lifetime ownership and exit code; fail unsent queued requests using the existing failure/callback route.
Fault survives daemon restart; explicit recovery is required. Initialized idle exits, active unknown work and verified terminal results retain existing behavior.

validation.red: New Pi empty-startup test failed before implementation: provider fault was not recorded.
test_repairs: Two new queued-task queries omitted required agent_name.
Initial callback test used a canned Lead response; an opt-in echo fixture now verifies actual continuation contains failed child status and fault details.

limits: No new real-model inference in this patch; earlier Pi/Claude live acceptance tested the preceding build.
This fixes confirmed pre-initialization process exit. A silent live startup or inherited open handles are not declared dead by timeout.
Initialized idle session recreation remains supported. A provider repeatedly exiting after successful initialization is outside this new pre-initialization fault classification.
Default Rust promotion still requires remaining interface/foreground and migration acceptance; native Herdr open currently accepts Pi/Codex terminal adapters.
